brief.title: Automotive Vehicles
brief.audience: M.Tech. Automotive Electronics students (Graduate level) - Engineering graduates with NO automotive or mechanical background
brief.notes: Comprehensive study of automotive vehicle systems with physics and mathematics foundation, covering powertrain, transmission, chassis dynamics, electrical systems, and safety systems Institution: BITS Pilani - M.Tech. Automotive Electronics. Credits: 3. Session length: 2 hours (90 min lecture + 30 min Q&A).

modules.title: Vehicle Motion Fundamentals
topics: Forces Acting on a Moving Vehicle
modules.note: Apply physics and mathematics to analyze vehicle motion, calculate force and power requirements, and understand tire-road interaction fundamentals Module outcome MO-1: Apply physics and mathematics to analyze vehicle motion, calculate force and power requirements, and understand tire-road interaction fundamentals

modules.title: Powertrain Systems
modules.note: Understand IC engine operation as a torque-generating device, analyze engine support systems, and compare power transmission mechanisms Module outcome MO-2: Understand IC engine operation as a torque-generating device, analyze engine support systems, and compare power transmission mechanisms

modules.title: Chassis Dynamics & Control
modules.note: Analyze vehicle dynamics using mathematical models and understand chassis control systems (braking, steering, suspension) Module outcome MO-3: Analyze vehicle dynamics using mathematical models and understand chassis control systems (braking, steering, suspension)

modules.title: Vehicle Electrical & Control Systems
modules.note: Understand vehicle electrical architecture, ECU-based control systems, and vehicle communication networks Module outcome MO-4: Understand vehicle electrical architecture, ECU-based control systems, and vehicle communication networks

modules.title: Vehicle Architecture & Comfort
modules.note: Understand complete vehicle architecture, body construction, HVAC systems, and passive safety systems Module outcome MO-5: Understand complete vehicle architecture, body construction, HVAC systems, and passive safety systems

modules.title: Active Safety & Emerging Technologies
modules.note: Understand active safety systems, introduction to ADAS, and emerging vehicle technologies Module outcome MO-6: Understand active safety systems, introduction to ADAS, and emerging vehicle technologies

objectives.text: Study main components/systems of an automobile (engine, transmission, drive-axle system, suspension system, brake system, etc.)
Understand fundamental working principles of different systems
Learn performance analysis along with working and important aspects of various components of automotive vehicles
Get acquainted with advanced concepts through projects and assignments

outcomes.text: Apply Newton's laws of motion to analyze forces acting on a moving vehicle
Calculate rolling resistance force using coefficient of rolling resistance and vehicle weight
Calculate aerodynamic drag force using drag coefficient, frontal area, and vehicle speed
Calculate gradient resistance force for vehicles on inclined surfaces
Determine total resistance force for different driving scenarios (level road, uphill, downhill, varying speeds)
Explain vehicle performance metrics (acceleration, top speed, gradeability) and their dependence on resistance forces
Identify tire construction types (radial, bias-ply) and explain tire nomenclature and specifications
Calculate normal force on tires and explain load distribution among wheels
Apply friction principles to calculate maximum tire force using coefficient of friction and normal load
Explain tire slip (longitudinal and lateral) and its relationship to tire force generation
Describe the friction circle concept and analyze combined braking and cornering forces
Explain factors affecting tire grip (tire pressure, temperature, road surface, tire wear)
Convert linear force at tire contact patch to torque at wheel using wheel radius relationship
Calculate wheel torque requirements for various driving conditions using force and radius
Apply rotational motion equations to convert torque and rotational speed to power requirements
Calculate vehicle acceleration performance (0-100 km/h time) using force, mass, and resistance
Determine maximum gradeability for a vehicle using available tractive force and vehicle weight
Calculate top speed of a vehicle by balancing available power with total resistance forces
Explain the internal combustion engine as a device that converts fuel energy into rotational torque
Identify major engine components (piston, cylinder, crankshaft, connecting rod, valves) and explain their mechanical functions
Describe the 4-stroke engine cycle (intake, compression, power, exhaust) from a mechanical perspective
Explain engine terminology (bore, stroke, displacement, compression ratio) and calculate engine capacity
Interpret engine torque and power curves and explain their relationship to vehicle performance
Classify IC engines based on fuel type (petrol/diesel), number of cylinders, and configuration (inline, V, flat)
Explain why engines generate heat and the need for effective cooling systems
Compare air-cooled and liquid-cooled systems and analyze their suitability for different applications
Identify cooling system components (radiator, thermostat, water pump, fan, coolant) and explain their operation
Explain the need for engine lubrication and the functions of engine oil (friction reduction, heat dissipation, cleaning)
Describe lubrication system components (oil pump, filter, oil galleries, sump) and oil circulation path
Explain engine oil specifications (viscosity grades like 5W-30, API/ACEA classifications) and selection criteria
Interpret engine performance maps (torque curve, power curve, BSFC map) and identify optimal operating regions
Explain the air-fuel mixture requirements for combustion and the stoichiometric ratio concept
Compare fuel delivery systems (carburetor vs fuel injection) and explain their basic operation
Describe Multi-Point Fuel Injection (MPFI) and Direct Injection (GDI) systems and their advantages
Explain air intake systems and the purpose of air filters, intake manifold, and throttle valve
Describe basic emission types (CO, HC, NOx, PM) and introduce emission control requirements (BS4, BS6)
Explain the need for transmission in matching engine output characteristics to wheel torque requirements
Calculate gear ratios and analyze their effect on torque multiplication and speed reduction
Describe clutch operation (single-plate, multi-plate) and explain engagement/disengagement mechanism
Explain manual gearbox construction (constant mesh, synchromesh) and gear shifting mechanism
Design basic transmission gear ratios for given vehicle performance requirements (acceleration vs top speed)
Analyze power flow through a manual transmission from engine to output shaft
Explain automatic transmission operation including torque converter and planetary gear sets
Compare transmission technologies (CVT, DCT/DSG, AMT) and their performance characteristics
Describe differential operation and its role in distributing power to wheels while allowing speed difference
Calculate final drive ratio and analyze its impact on vehicle performance and fuel economy
Compare powertrain configurations (FWD, RWD, AWD, 4WD) and explain their advantages and limitations
Introduce electric powertrains (motor, battery, inverter) and compare torque characteristics with IC engines
Identify forces and moments acting on a vehicle during acceleration, braking, and cornering
Calculate longitudinal acceleration performance using available tractive force and vehicle mass
Analyze load transfer during acceleration and calculate front/rear axle load distribution changes
Analyze load transfer during braking and calculate front/rear axle load distribution changes
Calculate lateral load transfer during cornering using centrifugal force and vehicle geometry
Explain the relationship between weight distribution and vehicle handling characteristics
Apply friction principles to calculate braking force using tire-road friction and normal load
Calculate braking deceleration and stopping distance for given braking force and vehicle mass
Describe hydraulic brake system components (master cylinder, brake booster, brake lines, calipers) and operation
Compare disc brakes and drum brakes and analyze their performance characteristics
Explain Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) operation and wheel slip control principle
Describe brake force distribution between front and rear axles and the role of proportioning valve
Explain Ackermann steering geometry and calculate inner and outer wheel steering angles for turn without slip
Calculate turning radius using wheelbase, steering angle, and Ackermann principle
Describe steering geometry parameters (caster, camber, toe, kingpin inclination) and their effects on handling
Compare steering mechanisms (rack-and-pinion vs recirculating ball) and calculate steering ratio
Explain power steering systems (hydraulic and Electric Power Assisted Steering - EPAS) and their operation
Describe steering feedback and explain the importance of steering feel for driver control
Apply spring-mass-damper system principles to analyze vehicle suspension behavior
Explain suspension functions (ride comfort, road holding, handling) and the trade-offs between them
Compare suspension types (independent vs dependent: McPherson strut, double wishbone, multi-link, solid axle)
Describe spring types (coil, leaf, torsion bar, air) and damper operation (twin-tube, monotube)
Explain anti-roll bar (stabilizer bar) operation and its effect on roll stiffness and cornering behavior
Describe electronic suspension systems (adaptive damping, air suspension) and their control strategies
Describe automotive electrical architecture and explain 12V and 24V system configurations
Explain battery technology (lead-acid, AGM) and analyze battery specifications (Ah capacity, CCA, reserve capacity)
Describe charging system components (alternator, voltage regulator) and explain voltage regulation and charging control
Explain starting system operation (starter motor, solenoid, bendix drive) and cranking power requirements
Compare automotive lighting technologies (halogen, HID, LED, matrix LED) and their control systems
Explain wiring system design, electrical load distribution, fuse and relay protection, and ground distribution
Explain the role of Electronic Control Unit (ECU) in modern vehicles and identify major ECU types
Describe engine management ECU functions (fuel control, ignition timing, air management, emissions)
Classify automotive sensors (temperature, pressure, position, speed, mass airflow, oxygen sensor) and explain their operation
Classify automotive actuators (fuel injectors, throttle valve, VVT solenoid, EGR valve) and explain their control
Explain closed-loop control principle in engine management (lambda/oxygen sensor feedback for air-fuel ratio control)
Describe transmission control unit (TCU) operation and automatic transmission shift control strategies
Explain the need for automotive communication networks and compare point-to-point vs networked architectures
Describe CAN (Controller Area Network) bus architecture, protocol layers, and message frame structure
Explain CAN bus arbitration mechanism, error detection, and fault confinement
Describe LIN (Local Interconnect Network) bus operation and its application in body electronics
Explain OBD-II (On-Board Diagnostics) standards, diagnostic trouble codes (DTC), and emission diagnostics
Analyze network topology design and calculate CAN bus load for given message traffic
Identify and classify different types of automobiles based on design (sedan, SUV, hatchback), application, and fuel type
Compare chassis types (monocoque/unibody, ladder frame, space frame) and analyze their applications and advantages
Describe body construction methods and material selection (steel, aluminum, composites) for vehicle structures
Calculate weight distribution (front/rear, left/right) and analyze its impact on vehicle performance and handling
Explain crash structures and crumple zones and their role in energy absorption and passenger safety
Describe the complete vehicle architecture and identify major subsystems and their physical locations
Explain HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning) system fundamentals and cabin comfort requirements
Describe the refrigeration thermodynamic cycle (compression, condensation, expansion, evaporation) with P-h diagram
Identify HVAC components (compressor, condenser, evaporator, expansion valve, refrigerant) and explain their operation
Compare compressor types (fixed displacement, variable displacement, electric compressor) and their control mechanisms
Explain heating system operation and its integration with engine cooling system (heater core)
Describe automatic climate control systems, multi-zone temperature management, and cabin air quality control
Explain crash safety principles and occupant protection strategies (crumple zones, safety cage, load paths)
Describe seatbelt systems (3-point, pretensioners, load limiters) and explain their operation and effectiveness
Explain airbag systems (frontal, side, curtain, knee airbags) and describe deployment strategies
Describe airbag control unit (ACU) operation, crash sensors (accelerometers), and deployment decision algorithms
Explain pedestrian protection systems (active hood lift, exterior airbags) and their activation mechanisms
Describe vehicle safety testing standards (NCAP, Euro NCAP, IIHS) and crash test evaluation criteria
Explain Electronic Stability Control (ESC) operation and yaw moment control during cornering and emergency maneuvers
Describe how ESC uses individual wheel braking to generate corrective yaw moment and stabilize the vehicle
Explain Traction Control System (TCS) operation and wheel slip control during acceleration on low-friction surfaces
Describe the integration of ESC, TCS, and ABS and explain how they work together for vehicle stability
Explain understeer and oversteer conditions and how ESC detects and corrects these behaviors
Describe Hill Start Assist (HSA) and Hill Descent Control (HDC) systems and their operation
Introduce Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and classify common features (ACC, LKA, AEB, BSD) - overview only
Describe Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) and Lane Keeping Assist (LKA) basic operation principles - brief introduction
Explain Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) and Blind Spot Detection (BSD) functionality - brief introduction
Identify sensor technologies for ADAS (camera, radar, ultrasonic, LiDAR) and their basic working principles
Explain SAE levels of vehicle autonomy (L0 to L5) and describe the current state of autonomous driving technology
Introduce emerging vehicle technologies (electric vehicles, connected vehicles, V2X communication) - brief overview
